282	name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
283	description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
284	metadata: 
285	  node_type: memory
286	  type: project
287	  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
288	  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
289	---
290	
291	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
292	
293	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
294	
295	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
296	
297	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
298	
299	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
300	
301	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
302	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
303	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
304	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
305	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
306	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
307	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
308	the harness had opened on the Acer.
309	
310	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
311	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
312	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
313	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
314	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
315	
316	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
317	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
318	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
319	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
320	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
321	concluding anything about the app.
322	
323	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
324	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
325	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
326	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
327	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
328	
329	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
330	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
331	`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
332	all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
333	directory — the directory alone is not enough.
334	
335	**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
336	
337	**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
338	
339	**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.
340	
341	**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
342	against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
343	first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
344	agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and

name: persistent-print-issues-spike
description: "2026-10-08 second-run spike: print issues outside chat work with zero upstream edits; where the prototype and report live, the native facts that shaped it, and the decisions still open"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Second run of the "persistent print issues" spike (2026-10-08). Kenneth called the first run (Codex, `investigation-persistent-print-issues.md` in the main checkout, producer hooks in Plater.cpp) "really bad" without saying why, and asked for an independent redo with a prototype pre-approved.

**Where it lives:** uncommitted in worktree `.claude/worktrees/wonderful-roentgen-83d009` (branch `claude/persistent-print-issues-spike-9238a1`). Report: `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2.md` there, evidence in the folder of the same name. Code: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/` (PrintIssueMonitor, IssueOverlay), `AgentHost::submit_issue_message`, harness modes `--print-issues`, `--print-issues-capture <dir>`, `--manual-print-issues`.

**Result:** end to end works with 0 lines changed in OrcaSlicer-owned files for the feature itself. The reader re-asks native checks instead of recording at producers.

**2026-10-09: converted to production work by Kenneth** ("ignore everything that said this is a temporary spike"). His decisions: hide ALL native notices; status pill in the canvas's lower right corner (where notices were), list opening upward; chat message quotes Orca's text. Upstream footprint is 2 added lines in `NotificationManager::render_notifications`: an early return when `wxGetApp().plater()->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden()` (Kenneth's idea: reuse the flag the shell already sets and restores; my first version added a 6-line dedicated switch). It asks the Prepare canvas, not the drawn canvas, because Check print is a second canvas without the flag and drew the notices again (tested). It sits after `sort_notifications()` because current upstream added `m_imgui_ready = true` at the top of the function (the merge simulation caught that). With no agent set up, a press sends nothing and a dialog offers setup (Kenneth's decision, 2026-10-09). A task chip was spawned for the four gaps hiding all notices leaves (operation notices, flushing-volume warning, future upstream warning kinds, readers never triggered at runtime). Uncommitted candidate passes: print-issues scenario 39 steps/336 checks in light and dark, shell regression 527, agent_bridge_tests 4756, jusprin_tests 584. Files no longer carry "spike" in their names: `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc`, `print_issues_agent.hpp`, `tests/jusprin/test_print_issues.cpp`.

Kenneth caught by hand that the bubble covered its object near the top edge; 324 green checks had missed it because nothing asserted "does not cover the object". Placement is now `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout` with unit tests.

**Native facts worth not rediscovering:**
- `Print::validate` is public and const; re-calling it on `PartPlate::fff_print()` costs under 1 ms. It holds one error and one warning at most.
- `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` (public) is true during the 500 ms before Orca applies an edit to the print; that is the "not yet validated" signal.
- `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is defined in Plater.cpp and declared nowhere. A `wxDECLARE_EVENT` in `JusPrin/Workspace/PlaterProjectState.hpp` (pulled into Plater.cpp by the `ProjectState.hpp` shim) gives it external linkage with no upstream edit.
- A copy over the plate edge is dropped from validation. A slice warning stays current after a plain move and goes non-current only when its step is invalidated. A move during a slice does not cancel it.
- Notification popups are not an issue list: dismissal removes them, targets are in closures, and they are not retired while the window is inactive.

**Still open (Kenneth's):** repeat presses; other plates; whether to run a live-model check; a JusPrin surface for operation notices (export finished, upload progress, network errors), which hiding all notices removed.

Related: [[agent-bridge-phase-3]], [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: worktree-session-cannot-write-main-checkout
description: "In a desktop-app worktree session a PreToolUse hook refuses Write/Edit to the main checkout; put reports in the worktree root (untracked) and tell Kenneth the path"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 a session running in `.claude/worktrees/<name>` tried to write a report next to its handoff in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/` and the Write tool was refused by a hook: edits to the base checkout "do not land on this session's branch and may corrupt the user's primary working copy". Bash `cp` is not stopped by the hook, but that is working around a deliberate guard, so anything copied there was moved back.

**Why:** handoffs are read from the main checkout ([[handoff-docs-not-committed]]), which makes it tempting to hand the report back in the same place.

**How to apply:** write reports and evidence folders in the worktree root, leave them untracked ([[temp-docs-stay-untracked-and-visible]]), and give Kenneth the worktree path. Never use the scratchpad for a deliverable; the app's file pane cannot open it as part of the project.

name: harness-gl-readback-capture
description: "When the Mac screen is locked the shell harness's screen-blit captures come back blank (2.8 KB PNGs); read the canvas's own pixels with glReadPixels(GL_FRONT) after render() instead"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`write_screen_capture` / `blit_screen` in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` photograph the desktop through `wxScreenDC`. With the screen locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` prints a line) every PNG is a blank ~2.8 KB file and no check fails.

For anything drawn inside the GL canvas (ImGui overlays, the tool strip, bubbles) read the frame back instead: `prepare_canvas().render()`, then `glReadBuffer(GL_FRONT)` and `glReadPixels` over `get_canvas_size()`, flip vertically into a `wxImage`, save as PNG. Worked on 2026-10-08 with the screen locked and the window inactive; needs `#include <glad/gl.h>`. Native notifications drawn by Orca are in the same frame, so they appear too. Web views still need `capture_web_view`.

Side effect of an inactive window: Orca's `NotificationManager::update_notifications` returns early, so closed popups are never retired and `get_notification_count()` only grows.

Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture]].

name: fake-bambu-printer-sim
description: "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.{hpp,cpp} — the in-process Bambu printer stand-in that IS on jusprin-newui (unlike the Moonraker simulator); keeps a real Bambu system preset selected and substitutes only the agent."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b5985db0-8e89-40a4-b560-5b7dcd439f2d
  modified: 2026-09-16T15:54:40.830Z
---

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.

**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

**How to apply:** For "fake a printer on jusprin-newui" requests, this is the one that's actually there — check `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/` first. See [[verify-current-branch-before-memory-recall]] for why this file exists: an earlier session answered "how do we fake a printer" from the Moonraker memory alone and missed this entirely, because it never grepped the current tree for "fake"/"Testing" before recalling.

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: bash-cwd-resets-after-background
description: "The Bash tool's working directory silently reverts to the primary repo after a run_in_background command or a failed cd; worktree commands must cd explicitly or use absolute paths."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3bfe66db-4c50-4102-b9b3-5ec3eab0060d
  modified: 2026-09-02T18:12:49.419Z
---

While working in a git worktree, a later `cmake --build build/arm64` and a
`git status` ran in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout)
instead of the worktree, so one build reported "no work to do" and a status
check looked as if every edit had been lost.

**Why:** After a `run_in_background` Bash call, and after a compound command
whose `cd` failed, the session cwd is the primary working directory again.
The tool result even says so, but it is easy to miss in a long session.

**How to apply:** In worktree sessions start every Bash command with
`cd <worktree> &&`, or use absolute paths everywhere (python patch scripts
with an absolute root are safest). Verify with `pwd` before trusting a
`git status` that looks wrong. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

6	
7	One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**
8	
9	- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
10	- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
11	- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.
12	
13	Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.
14	
15	## The ten principles
16	
17	### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much
18	
19	**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.
20	
21	**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.
22	
23	**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?
24	
25	**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.
26	
27	### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge
28	
29	**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.
30	
31	**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.
32	
33	**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?
34	
35	**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.
36	
37	### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it
38	
39	**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.
40	
41	**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.
42	
43	**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?
44	
45	**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.
46	
47	### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism
48	
49	**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.
50	
51	**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.
52	
53	**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?
54	
55	**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.
56	
57	### 5. One seam beats many touch points
58	
59	**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.
60	
61	**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.
62	
63	**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?
64	
65	**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.
66	
67	### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict
68	
69	**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.
70	
71	**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.
72	
73	**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.
74	
75	**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.
76	
77	### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly
78	
79	**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.
80	
81	**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.
82	
83	**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?
84	
85	**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.
86	
87	### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went
88	
89	**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.
90	
91	**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.
92	
93	**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?
94	
95	**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.
96	
97	### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it
98	
99	**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.
100	
101	**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.
102	
103	**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?
104	
105	**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.
106	
107	### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit
108	
109	**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.
110	
111	**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.
112	
113	**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?
114	
115	**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.
116	
117	## Before you finish
118	
119	A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:
120	
121	1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.
122	
123	   ```bash
124	   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
125	   ```
126	
127	   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.
128	
129	2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.
130	
131	3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.
132	
133	An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.
134	
135	## This fork's terrain
136	
137	Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.
138	
139	`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.
140	
141	Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.
142	
143	`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
144	upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
145	updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
146	or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
147	error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
148	strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
149	controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
150	print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
151	into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
152	19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
153	needed edits across eight upstream files.
154	
155	The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
156	after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
157	Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
158	correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
159	Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
160	fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
161	Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
162	no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
163	replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
164	addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
165	`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
166	on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
167	must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.
168	
169	Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
170	screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
171	availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
172	selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
173	Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
174	page, silently.
175	
176	Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
177	function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
178	sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
179	`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
180	and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
181	without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
182	owned by Plater's event handler.
183	
184	Historical measurements and the incidents behind several of these rules are in the [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) and, for the spike era, in the [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

10	
11	Kenneth converted the spike into production work and made three decisions. This section is current; everything below it describes the first prototype and is kept for its findings. Where the two disagree, this section wins.
12	
13	**Decisions taken**
14	
15	- OrcaSlicer's own notices are hidden entirely while the JusPrin shell is installed.
16	- The compact status sits in the lower right corner of the Prepare canvas, where those notices were. Its list opens upward.
17	- The chat message quotes OrcaSlicer's text under the request sentence.
18	
19	**Upstream footprint: 2 added lines, 0 changed, in 1 file.** In `NotificationManager::render_notifications`, after `sort_notifications()`:
20	
21	```cpp
22		if (wxGetApp().plater()->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden())
23			return;
24	```
25	
26	- It reuses the flag the shell already sets on the Prepare canvas at install and restores when the person switches back to the classic presentation, so there is no new member, setter or getter, and nothing new to save or restore. An earlier version of this work added a dedicated switch (6 lines in 2 files); Kenneth pointed out the existing flag covers it.
27	- It asks the Prepare canvas, not the canvas being drawn. The version that asked the drawn canvas (`canvas.legacy_overlays_hidden()`) was built and tested first: the Check print window is a second canvas whose own flag is never set, and it drew 7 notice windows there. Setting the flag on that canvas instead would also remove Check print's own stock controls. With the Prepare canvas as the question, Check print draws none.
28	- Skipping the draw does not disturb the notices' lifetimes: those advance in `update_notifications`, not in the draw.
29	- Rebase evidence: fork base `3ffb9585d2`, upstream `b3490a1cdc`, candidate commit object `6e97ea01e8` (on no branch). The conflict list is identical to the baseline's (3,890 both); `NotificationManager.cpp` has one conflict block before and after. In the merged result upstream's new `m_imgui_ready = true;` line runs first, then `sort_notifications()`, then the early return.
30	- The simulation is why the lines sit after `sort_notifications()` and not at the top of the function: at the top they collided with that new upstream line, and the wrong resolution would have skipped it.
31	- Upstream changes at the touched lines since the fork base and in two years: 1 and 1.
32	- What the fork owns: two lines that read an existing fork flag. No upstream line deleted or rewritten.
33	
34	**What changed from the prototype**
35	
36	- The reader now also covers OrcaSlicer's plate checks (TPU count, filament printability, PLA with PETG, nozzle and filament, filament mixture, prime tower outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach) and the post-slice checks (path outside the plate or above the print height, nozzle range and height errors, filament not printable on the plate). All through public OrcaSlicer functions or state.
37	- "Ask AI may only read" is now enforced by the chat host itself, not only by the model provider adapter.
38	- Typed messages and button messages share one path in the chat host.
39	- The two bubble widths are tokens with guards. All strings go through translation.
40	- Bubble and status placement is a separate unit with its own tests.
41	- The long list scrolls instead of leaving the canvas.
42	- With no assistant set up, a press of either button sends nothing to the chat. A dialog says "The AI assistant isn't set up yet. Set it up in the chat panel, and it can explain this issue and help you fix it." with **Set up now** (opens the chat panel's setup) and **Not now**.
43	- Docs: a "Print issues" section in `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md` and the native findings in `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`.
44	
45	**Verification on the candidate**
46	
47	| Check | Result |
48	|---|---|
49	| `jusprin_tests` (includes 9 new layout and message tests) | 584 assertions pass |
50	| `agent_bridge_tests` (includes 5 new chat-path tests) | 4,756 assertions pass |
51	| OrcaSlicer's notices drawn on the Prepare canvas and in Check print (counted from the frame) | 0 and 0, while OrcaSlicer holds notices underneath |
52	| `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests` (new token guards) | pass; one pre-existing expected failure unrelated to this work |
53	| Real-app print-issues scenario, light | 42 steps, 354 checks, 0 failures |
54	| Real-app print-issues scenario, dark | 354 checks, 0 failures |
55	| Existing shell scenario | 529 checks, 0 failures |
56	| Switch to classic presentation | flag restored, so notices are drawn again; 31 checks, 0 failures |
57	| Chat page type check | clean |
58	
59	**Consequences of hiding every notice, which Kenneth accepted and should know the extent of**
60	
61	- Operation notices have no JusPrin surface yet and are no longer seen: export finished, upload and download progress, update available, network and sync errors, tips, the object size card. Slicing progress and cancel remain in the header.
62	- A print warning the reader does not cover is shown nowhere. Known today: "flushing volume set to 0", whose check is private to the canvas class. A warning kind upstream adds later is in the same position until a reader is written; the architecture guide says what to check after an upstream update.
63	- The new plate-check and post-slice readers are verified by build and by code reading only. None of their conditions was reproduced at runtime, because the test printer has one nozzle and no TPU.
64	
65	**Still not done**
66	
67	- Live model behaviour for either button.
68	- Windows and Linux.
69	- Nothing is committed.
70	
71	## The answer
72	
73	**Can we keep current print issues visible and actionable outside chat without taking ownership of Orca's warning logic?** Yes. Demonstrated at runtime, not only argued from code.
74	
75	**What native access is missing?** Nothing that needs an upstream edit. One native fact, the reason a slice failed, exists only inside an event that OrcaSlicer defines in `Plater.cpp` and declares in no header. A declaration placed in a fork-owned header that `Plater.cpp` already includes makes that event observable. Upstream line count: 0.
76	
77	**What would the fork permanently own?**
78	
79	- A *reader* that asks OrcaSlicer's own checks what is wrong, and decides when to ask again. It owns no rule about what counts as a problem.
80	- The list of native sources it reads (six today, see the table). A new kind of native warning is invisible until someone adds a reader for it. This is the real permanent cost.
81	- The pill, list and bubble on the canvas, and their layout rules.
82	- One chat entry point for a message sent by a button outside the page, plus the "explain only" tool limit.
83	- The tests that pin all of the above to OrcaSlicer's behaviour.
84	
85	## What was built
86	
87	Uncommitted, in worktree `.claude/worktrees/wonderful-roentgen-83d009` (branch `claude/persistent-print-issues-spike-9238a1`, at `jusprin-newui` commit `198c64606f`). 17 files, none of which exists in upstream. About 1,050 lines of product code and 1,050 lines of test code.
88	
89	| Piece | File | What it does |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| Issue reader | `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor.{hpp,cpp}` | Builds the current issue list for the active plate from native state. Recomputes on five existing signals. |
92	| Canvas overlay | `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/IssueOverlay.{hpp,cpp}` | Status pill, issue list, and the anchored bubble with both buttons. Drawn with ImGui through the overlay hook the tool strip already uses. |
93	| Chat entry | `Agent/AgentHost.{hpp,cpp}`, `AgentProtocol.hpp`, `ProjectStateDocument.cpp` | `submit_issue_message`: a durable user message with structured context attached. |
94	| Wiring | `Shell/ShellController.{hpp,cpp}`, `CanvasPresentationController.{hpp,cpp}` | Builds the context at click time and hands it to the chat. |
95	| Event declaration | `Workspace/PlaterProjectState.hpp` | Makes the slice-completed event observable. |
96	| Test scenario | `tests/shell/print_issues_spike_scenario.inc`, `print_issues_spike_agent.hpp`, 52 lines in `shell_harness.cpp` | `--print-issues`, `--print-issues-capture <dir>`, `--manual-print-issues`. |
97	
98	Screenshots and the run log are in `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2/`. The pictures are the canvas's own pixels read back from OpenGL, so they are what was drawn, not a mock-up.
99	
100	## Verdicts
101	
102	### Anchored, clickable overlay: verified working
103	
104	- **Rendering owner.** ImGui inside the Prepare canvas's own frame, through `GLCanvas3D::set_overlay_renderer`. That hook is an existing fork seam. No web content over the GL canvas, no extra window.
105	- **Position.** The anchor is the top centre of the target copy's bounding box, projected with the camera every frame. Nothing about position is stored. The test computes the projection separately and compares: equal to within 1.5 px after orbit, zoom, window resize and object move.
106	- **Clicks.** Real pointer events through the canvas's mouse handler and ImGui's hit test press both buttons, the pager and a list row. ImGui takes the pointer first, so a click on the bubble never reaches selection or the camera.
107	- **Beside, never on top.** The bubble goes above the object when there is room. Otherwise it takes the object's right, left or underside, whichever fits inside the canvas without covering the object, the pill, the open list or the tool strip. The first version only slid the bubble down to fit and covered the object when it was near the top of the view; Kenneth caught that by hand on 2026-10-09. A test now reproduces it (it failed before the fix) and passes (`issues-05c-object-near-top.png`).
108	- **Edges.** When the object is off screen or behind the camera, or fills the view so no side is free, the bubble docks under the pill rather than disappearing.
109	- **Highlight.** Selecting an issue selects its copy through the existing `select_copy` command, by OrcaSlicer's instance ID. With two objects of the same name, the right one is selected.
110	
111	Not verified: display scaling other than this Mac's 2x, Windows and Linux, dark mode, gizmo dragging while a bubble is open.
112	
113	### Existing chat submission: verified working, with fork-owned additions
114	
115	Path traced and exercised: button click → `ShellController::submit_issue` → `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` → message appended to the project document → `message_added` to the page → `begin_reply` → `AgentRequest`.
116	
117	- The message is an ordinary user message. The real chat page drew it with no page change (`08-asked-chat.png`).
118	- The structured context travels beside the text and reaches the model as labelled source data. Fields sent: issue id, source, severity, native code, setting key, Orca's message; target scope, object ID, copy ID, object name, plate ID; whether Orca has validated, the evidence generation, sliced and slicing flags; workspace session ID and revision. The whole workspace snapshot already goes with every request.
119	- The composer draft is left alone. The closed chat pane is opened.
120	- **Missing before this prototype:** any way for native UI to send a user message, and any place on a message to carry context. Both are fork-owned additions (about 70 lines).
121	
122	### End to end: verified
123	
124	Warning appears → object highlights → bubble tracks the object and view → each button submits the right visible message and context → native revalidation updates or removes the bubble. Also verified with object deletion and with several issues at once. 334 checks, 0 failures.
125	
126	## Source and coverage table
127	
128	"Re-asked" means the reader calls the same public native function OrcaSlicer calls. "Read" means it reads state OrcaSlicer already stores.
129	
130	| Native source | Example reproduced | Blocks printing natively? | Where the truth lives | Target identity | Goes stale / clears | Prototype |
131	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
132	| `Print::validate` error | Two cubes 2 mm apart with "By object" sequence; vase mode with two objects | Yes. Plate marked invalid, Slice disabled | Not stored. Re-asked on the plate's `Print` | Copy ID, object ID, or none plus a setting key | Stale for up to 500 ms after an edit; cleared by Orca's next validation | Verified |
133	| `Print::validate` warning | The handoff's "is too close to others" (by-layer mode) | No | Not stored. Re-asked | Copy ID of the first offender only | Same | Verified |
134	| Copy over the plate edge | Cube straddling the edge | Yes | `ModelInstance::print_volume_state`, read | Copy ID | Same | Verified |
135	| Slicing step warnings | "has floating cantilever" on an overhang | No | `Print` and `PrintObject` step state, with Orca's own `current` flag, read | Object ID | Orca marks it not current when its step is invalidated; removed by the next slice | Verified |
136	| Slice result | "Found gcode path conflicts between…" | No | `Print::get_conflict_result`, slice result warnings, read | Copy ID or none | Gone when the slice is invalidated | Verified (conflict). G-code processor warnings are read but none was reproduced |
137	| Slicing failure | "No layers were detected" on a 0.02 mm slab | Yes | **Only in the completion event** | Object ID when the error carries one; this one does not | Stale when the project changes; dropped when a slice starts | Verified |
138	| Plate checks the canvas runs | Filament, TPU, nozzle and mixture compatibility | Some | Public `PartPlate::check_*` functions, re-askable | Plate-wide | Same as validation | **Not prototyped.** Building block confirmed in code only |
139	| Post-slice bounds | Toolpath beyond plate or height | Yes | Slice result; the fork's `slice_report` already recomputes one | Plate-wide | With the slice | **Not prototyped** |
140	| Operation errors | Network and download errors pushed as notifications | n/a | Notification only | n/a | n/a | Verified absent from the list |
141	
142	The "unfamiliar warning" case needs no special handling: the reader has no explanation for any warning. Every entry is Orca's own text plus identifiers, so an unknown one is carried the same way as a known one.
143	
144	## Native behaviour that shapes the design
145	
146	Each of these was observed at runtime or read in code, and each changes what the product can promise.
147	
148	1. **OrcaSlicer's validation holds one error and one warning at most.** A later check overwrites an earlier warning (`Print.cpp:1261` has a FIXME saying so). Several offending objects become one message with several lines and one target. "Several validation findings on one object" cannot happen natively.
149	2. **A copy over the plate edge is dropped from validation.** With both overlapping cubes over the edge, Orca reported two placement blockers and no clearance warning.
150	3. **A slice warning survives a plain move.** Moving the object invalidates the slice result but not the step that produced the warning, so Orca still vouches for it. Changing the setting the step depends on (`enable_support`) makes it not current. Only the next slice removes it.
151	4. **A move made during a slice does not cancel it.** Orca's log shows `apply result=1` (changed, not invalidated) and the slice finished valid. The reader reports Orca's verdict; it does not second-guess it.
152	5. **Popups are not a list of issues.** Closing a popup removes it while the issue stays true (`issues-07-popup-dismissed.png`). Orca merges slicing warnings that share a message ID into one popup across objects. Targets are captured inside callbacks and cannot be read. Popups are not retired at all while the window is inactive (the count grew from 3 to 10 in one run).
153	6. **Orca applies an edit to the print on a 500 ms timer.** Until then the print describes the old project. `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` is public and tells the reader exactly this. It is what makes "checking" distinguishable from "no issues".
154	7. **Validation exists only for the active plate.** Other plates are unknown until visited.
155	8. **The warning's `type` field is uninitialised in some producers** (`StringObjectException warningtemp;` in `Print.cpp`). The reader reports a type only when it is one Orca defines, and never uses it for identity.
156	9. **Validation costs 0.2 to 0.9 ms** on these fixtures, so asking a second time is cheap here. Not measured on a large plate.
157	
158	## Lifecycle results
159	
160	All from `investigation-persistent-print-issues-run2/harness-run.log`.
161	
162	| Case | Result |
163	|---|---|
164	| Creation | Issue appears after Orca's own validation, with copy ID |
165	| Repeated updates | Same issue ID after each revalidation; no duplicates |
166	| Popup dismissed | Issue stays |
167	| Edit, before Orca revalidates | List marked stale, pill says "Checking…", buttons off, a forced submit returns `unchecked` |
168	| Fix, then revalidation | Issue and bubble removed. No "No print issues" shown before the check |
169	| Undo / redo | Undo brings back the same issue ID on the same copy; redo clears it |
170	| Object deleted with its bubble open | Its issues go at once, before revalidation; bubble closes; submit returns `expired` |
171	| Plate switch | List follows the active plate and returns on switching back |
172	| Project replaced | New session, empty list; an old issue ID cannot be submitted |
173	| Slice warning, remedy applied, not yet resliced | Shown stale; cannot be submitted; removed only by the new slice |
174	| Slice fails | Reason listed as a blocker; stale after an edit |
175	| Edit during a slice | Reader matches Orca's final verdict; no false failure |
176	| Duplicate object names | Correct copy selected by ID |
177	| Several issues | Three issues on two objects; one bubble pages through both findings on one object; the list shows all |
178	| Plate-wide issue | Docked bubble labelled "Whole plate"; no object invented |
179	| Object near the top edge, no room above | Bubble placed below the object; does not cover it or the tool strip |
180	| Chat pane closed | Opened on submit |
181	| Reply running | Buttons off; a forced press sends nothing; the host itself queues a message that arrives mid-reply |
182	| Agent unavailable | Status keeps working; the question is kept and the reply fails visibly with `agent_unavailable` |
183	| Same button pressed twice, nothing changed | One message |
184	
185	Regression: the existing shell scenario passes with the prototype (526 checks), and `agent_bridge_tests` passes (4,691 assertions).
186	
187	## Intent and permissions
188	
189	- **Ask AI** sends "Explain this issue and my options." with `intent: explain`. For that turn the request names only the tools whose registry class is read-only (13 today). `OpenAIResponsesAgent` uses that list both to advertise tools and to refuse a call to any other (`OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:298`). So the limit is enforced by the app, not by wording.
190	- **Resolve with AI** sends "Help fix this issue." with `intent: resolve` and the ordinary tool set. It adds no tool and removes no check.
191	- A follow-up typed by the person is a normal turn with normal tools.
192	
193	Gaps: the limit is applied by the provider adapter, not by `AgentHost` itself, so another adapter would have to honour it too. A host-level refusal is a small hardening step. I did not run a live model, so how well the model uses the context, and whether its words stay within "explain", is unverified. That needs an API key and sends project data to the provider, which I did not do without being asked.
194	
195	## Options compared
196	
197	Fork base `3ffb9585d2`, upstream `b3490a1cdc` (local `upstream/main`, not re-fetched).
198	
199	| Option | Upstream lines | Upstream sites | Upstream changes at those sites since the fork base / in 2 years | Meets the requirements? |
200	|---|---|---|---|---|
201	| **1. Read native state and re-ask native checks (prototype)** | 0 | 0 | n/a | Yes, as tested |
202	| 1b. Same, declaring the event in `Plater.hpp` | 2 | 2 | 0 / 0 on those lines | Yes. Measured: adds one conflict block against current upstream, resolved by keeping both |
203	| 2. Read the notification manager | about 15 | 1 new accessor | `push_notification_data`: 2 / 3 | No. Loses targets, loses dismissed issues, merges objects |
204	| 3. Record results at the producers | 22 added, 3 removed in the first run's prototype, 9 hunks in `Plater.cpp` | `update_background_process`, `validate_current_plate`, `on_process_completed` | 2 / 10, 3 / 13, 6 / 7 | Likely yes, at a recurring rebase cost in the busiest file the fork touches |
205	
206	Option 3's numbers are a measurement of the first run's uncommitted diff, not a review of it.
207	
208	What option 1 depends on, and how it fails if upstream changes it:
209	
210	- `Print::validate`'s signature and `PartPlate::fff_print()`. Compile error.
211	- `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` staying a non-static definition in `Plater.cpp`. Compile or link error.
212	- `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()`. Compile error. Unchanged upstream for at least two years.
213	- `get_object_clashed_text()`, declared in no header. Link error.
214	- The meaning of the 500 ms timer. **Silent** if upstream replaces the timer with something else: the reader would call unchecked state checked. The lifecycle test "no all-clear before revalidation" is the guard.
215	- Any step upstream adds before or after its own validation call. **Silent**, text-only drift between the popup and the bubble.
216	
217	Merge simulation, `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=3ffb9585d2 upstream/main <commit>`: the baseline (`198c64606f`) has 3,890 conflicts, almost all inherited release-branch history. With the final prototype (commit object `61c2352356`, on no branch) the conflict list is identical. None of the 17 changed files exists in upstream.
218	
219	## Proposed behaviour
220	
221	Required:
222	
223	- One compact status that says one of three things: checking, no issues, or N issues with the number that block. Never "no issues" while Orca has not validated.
224	- A list of every issue, opened from the status.
225	- One bubble at a time, for the selected issue, beside its object and never covering it. All findings on that object share the bubble through a pager.
226	- A docked bubble for plate-wide issues and for objects out of view.
227	- Both buttons off while Orca has not validated the latest edit and while a reply is running.
228	- Context resolved at the click. Expired and unchecked issues are not sent.
229	- Orca's words shown unchanged.
230	
231	Optional polish: an edge arrow toward an off-screen object, plain-language rewrites of Orca's text, a context chip on the chat message instead of the quoted text.
232	
233	The prototype's pill sits on the canvas. The product home for the compact status is the header's status row, which already has the button and menu pieces. That is ordinary UI work, not a feasibility question, and I did not build it.
234	
235	## Smallest implementation scope
236	
237	1. Promote the reader, with the two unprototyped sources added.
238	2. Header status control in place of the canvas pill.
239	3. The bubble, to the design system. It uses theme colours and button recipes now, but two widths are literals that need tokens, and the text is ImGui's default font.
240	4. `submit_issue_message` plus a host-level check of the explain-only limit.
241	5. Turn the 39-step scenario into a kept harness mode.
242	
243	Acceptance tests: the lifecycle table above, each row as a harness check, plus the two silent-drift guards named under option 1.
244	
245	## Decisions for Kenneth
246	
247	1. **Where the compact status lives.** Header (recommended) or canvas.
248	2. **What the visible chat message contains.** The prototype quotes Orca's message under the fixed sentence so the chat reads sensibly later. The alternative is the fixed sentence plus a chip, which needs page work.
249	3. **Agent unavailable.** The prototype follows existing chat behaviour: the question is kept and the reply fails with a retry. The alternative is disabled buttons with a route to agent setup.
250	4. **Pressing the same button again with nothing changed.** The prototype treats it as the same question and sends nothing.
251	5. **Other plates.** Show only the active plate (prototype), or mark the others "not checked".
252	6. **Whether to run a live-model check.** It needs your API key and sends the test project to the provider.
253	
254	## Not verified
255	
256	- Live model behaviour for either button.
257	- Windows, Linux, dark mode, other display scales.
258	- The two unprototyped sources in the table.
259	- Large plates (validation cost, bubble overlap with many objects).
260	- A slicing failure that names its object. The one reproduced carries no object ID natively.
261	- A click landing in the same event-loop turn as a committed move. In that turn neither native flag is set yet. Real input cannot reach it, because the click handler is queued behind the move's own event; this is reasoning, not a test.
262	
263	## Reproduce
264	
265	Build `shell_integration_harness` in the worktree, then run with a scratch `HOME`:
266	
267	```bash
268	build/arm64/tests/shell/RelWithDebInfo/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --print-issues-capture <output-dir>
269	```
270	
271	`--manual-print-issues` leaves two overlapping cubes open for hands-on use.
